A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Time-MoE and Time-300B research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable matching across revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting, ablation, scaling, expert-activation, and computational-efficiency results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds Global Temp and TaxiBJ evaluations and further baseline comparisons, including Tables 14–16.

M1.justification: The intended architecture, shared and routed experts, training losses, multi-resolution heads, and greedy forecasting design are retained. Corrections to equations and scheduling pseudocode resolve inconsistencies in that existing description; they do not establish a redesigned or newly implemented method.

E1.justification: Global Temp replaces Electricity throughout the principal evaluations and associated analyses. Appendix D.3 additionally introduces short-term urban-flow forecasting on TaxiBJ, extending evaluation beyond the earlier long-term tasks. The Time-300B training collection remains unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 15–16 add reported comparisons with Timer at three pretraining-data scales, TFT, and N-BEATS. Timer was named in v1 but had no corresponding reported experimental results. These additions extend the existing comparison groups; the main comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The added TaxiBJ evaluation specifies 512-point contexts and horizons of 1, 8, 24, and 48. Table 11 additionally evaluates component ablations using MAE. Existing long-term context/horizon pairs, training configurations, and one-epoch fine-tuning remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Global Temp replaces Electricity in component and precision analyses, the expert-gating visualization, and the qualitative forecasting case study. The underlying ablation, scaling, precision, and expert-count questions remain the same; TaxiBJ and additional baseline scores do not introduce new robustness tests.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added results retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Global Temp results replace Electricity entries, aggregate results are revised, Table 11 adds MAE values, and Tables 14–16 introduce TaxiBJ and additional baseline results. Matched ETT and Weather entries in Tables 3–4 are unchanged. For example, Time-MoE-ultra's average zero-shot MSE changes from 0.302 to 0.322 across different benchmark suites, not as a same-setting performance decline.

T1.justification: Equations 7–8 correct the shared-gate parameter index from N to N+1 and use the normalized state in the routing score. Algorithm 1 changes its required horizon ordering from descending to ascending, making reverse iteration consistent with the stated greedy rule. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The introduction revises claimed average forecasting-error reductions from 23% to 20% for zero-shot evaluation and from 25% to 24% for in-distribution evaluation, following the benchmark replacement. The central contributions concerning sparse forecasting, 2.4-billion-parameter scaling, Time-300B, and computational efficiency remain.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning scaling, expert specialization, multi-resolution forecasting, Huber loss, and computational efficiency are retained. The expanded routing discussion elaborates the existing load-balancing rationale; no substantive new limitation or applicability boundary is introduced.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds a cleaning-code listing with previously unspecified details, including 128-point windows and a 256-point minimum subsequence length for window filtering. Appendix B expands implementation explanations, and new benchmarks receive construction or split information. These are documentation additions; existing training settings and resource disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix A newly acknowledges concurrent Moirai-MoE and distinguishes its expert/routing design and scale. Additional references include TimeMixer++, time-series scaling-law research, and sources for added datasets and comparisons. The broader research positioning remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized paragraph rewrites, expanded implementation and cleaning explanations, and a new Appendix D.3 for additional experiments. The principal section sequence and narrative remain intact. Conference headers, author markers, and terminology also receive small edits.

P2.justification: v3 adds a causal-attention schematic, three experimental tables, and a code listing; Table 11 gains MAE columns. Plot axes and benchmark panels are updated, and the Electricity showcase is replaced. The architecture diagram and five existing forecast showcases are retained, with limited overall layout changes.

improvement.justification: The new short-term TaxiBJ evaluation and actual Timer/TFT/N-BEATS comparisons strengthen evidence for the existing forecasting claims. Corrected scheduling and fuller cleaning documentation improve methodological clarity. These gains are limited by the unexplained removal of Electricity evaluation and questionable Timer aggregates: Table 15 reports 0.394 MSE for Timer-1B, whereas its six displayed dataset means average about 0.442, without an alternative aggregation explanation.
